svg.title: The disposition writer's stored-is-None branch holds two refusals, and each is now pinned by a case whose control turns red
svg.desc: Left: the command resolves the run's own head from the live pointer's tree when a pointer exists and from the run's ledger row or stored review when it does not, then reads the review store for that head. When a record carries the head the call is accepted and the disposition is written on the record the reader selected; when none carries it, the branch reached is stored-is-None, which holds two refusals. Refusal A: a record for the run describes another revision, so the refusal names both revisions. Refusal B: the store holds no record for the run at all, so the refusal names the missing record. Both leave the sub-floor row standing. Below: a scratch copy of the module with refusal A deleted. Against the base test file the whole file still passes, so the deleted branch was reached by nothing; against the test file this change adds, the mismatched-head case fails and reports refusal B's text.
svg.text: The stored-is-None branch holds two refusals; each now has a case
The head is resolved, the store is read for it, and what the store answers decides which refusal speaks.
crew dispose --run <id>
resolve the run’s own head
live pointer’s tree, else its records
select the review for that
head (head-first reader)
a record carries the head
accepted: written on that record
none carries it — stored is None
refusal A: a record describes another revision
the head-first reader selects nothing, while a record for
the run names a revision the work is not at
names both revisions · exits non-zero · row stands
case: a review keyed to the run’s base revision
refusal B: the store holds no record for the run
nothing was ever stored for it, so no record exists
for a disposition to be written against
names the missing record · exits non-zero · row stands
case: a live run whose store holds no record
the control that shows the cases can fail
A scratch copy deletes refusal A from the module; the same mutation is run against both test files.
base test file — 15 passed, EXIT=0: the deleted branch was reached by nothing.
head test file — 1 failed: the mismatched-head case, reporting refusal B’s text. EXIT=1
